meta.spec_reference: PNG (Portable Network Graphics) Specification Version 1.2 (libpng.org/pub/png/spec/1.2/, the version this template states it was written to at lines 20-21); APNG Specification 1.0 (wiki.mozilla.org/APNG_Specification, cited at lines 23-24) for acTL/fcTL/fdAT; RFC 1950 (zlib) and RFC 1951 (DEFLATE) for the IDAT, zTXt, compressed-iTXt, iCCP and fdAT payloads; CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (ISO 3309 / ITU-T V.42, the polynomial PNG 1.2 s.5.1.2 mandates) for the chunk CRC; RFC 3066 for iTXt language tags.

schema_extensions.name: underlying_type
schema_extensions.why: Enum-typed fields are declared with a typedef name (PNG_COLOR_SPACE_TYPE, APNG_DISPOSE_OP, ...) whose storage width only appears in the `typedef enum <byte>` line; this records the width so the rewrite step emits one byte, not four.

schema_extensions.name: declared_at
schema_extensions.why: When `evidence` cites the guard or the Checksum call that proves the constraint (line 367 for the signature, line 335 for the CRC), this also carries the declaration line and its verbatim snippet, so both are traceable.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.why: Records the individual values a format declares invalid (0 for width and height, 1/5/7 for color_type, 3/5/6/7/9-15 for bit depth) without implying any other bound on the field. It never expresses a span, so it cannot narrow a Tier C field beyond what the spec itself excludes.

schema_extensions.name: valid_values on a pattern_constraint entry
schema_extensions.why: The legal set of chunk names is a pattern rather than a finite list; the registered names are still listed so the rewrite step has a concrete vocabulary, with the pattern recorded as authoritative.

schema_extensions.name: then.field / then.fields / then.section / then.required / then.forbidden / then.position / then.tier / then.type / then.valid_values / then.completeness / then.required_value / then.required_value_hex / then.pattern / then.algorithm / then.covers / then.includes_self / then.endianness / then.codec / then.must_produce / then.content_is_free / then.derives_from
schema_extensions.why: The base schema only sketches `then`; PNG's conditional rules need the same typed vocabulary as `constraints` (a fixed chunk length per type, a zlib payload that applies only to IDAT, iCCP and compressed iTXt, section-level required/forbidden for PLTE and acTL).

schema_extensions.name: when.and / when.not_in
schema_extensions.why: PNG's chunk rules are keyed on two fields at once (chunk type plus IHDR color_type, as in tRNS, bKGD and sBIT) and on 'any type outside this set' for the opaque-data case; the base schema offers equals/in/min/max/present/absent only.

schema_extensions.name: length_prefix
schema_extensions.why: PNG's chunk envelope is a self-describing length-prefixed record (length, type, data, crc) and no base rule value says so; it is the rule that tells the rewrite step to build the data before writing its byte count.

schema_extensions.name: name / tier / must_emit_full_legal_set / also_covers / how_varied / diversity_budget / notes
schema_extensions.why: Per-field axes need a stable short name, the tier they protect, an explicit instruction to emit the whole legal set for Tier B fields, coverage of sibling fields that share one axis (the thirteen sBIT arms, the six tIME fields), and a sampling instruction that is not a bound.

schema_extensions.name: unused_declarations
schema_extensions.why: PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA is declared in the .bt but never instantiated, so there is no iCCP dispatch; recording that stops the rewrite step from inventing a struct the parser does not use, while the iCCP payload rule stays on a dependency.

schema_extensions.name: axis_coverage
schema_extensions.why: Names the few constraint keys that deliberately have no diversity axis of their own (single-legal-value enums and the CTYPE union alias), so the omission is visible as a decision; every Tier C field and every payload derives_from field does have one.

meta.structure_note: A PNG file is an 8-byte signature followed by a dense series of self-describing chunks, each `length(4) | type(4) | data(length) | crc(4)` in big-endian order, which the template dispatches on the 4-character type into a per-chunk struct and otherwise reads as `ubyte data[length]`; the only ordering rules are IHDR first and IEND last, and this format's payload well-formedness problem is the zlib stream carried by the IDAT chain (plus zTXt, compressed iTXt, iCCP profiles and APNG fdAT frames), which the .bt declares as an opaque byte array and never describes.

axis_coverage.reason: Each of these carries exactly one legal value, or is a union alias of a field that does have an axis, so an axis would add no sampling instruction: the constraint entry is the entire rule. Every Tier C field and every field named in a payload_wellformedness.derives_from has its own axis.

unused_declarations.name: PNG_ICCP_CHUNK_DATA
unused_declarations.note: Declared (string profile_name; ubyte red;) but never instantiated: iCCP is absent from the dispatch chain at lines 301-330, so an iCCP chunk is read as PNG_CHUNK.data. No constraints entry is emitted for it; the iCCP zlib rule lives on a dependency instead.

unused_declarations.name: readCTYPE / readIHDR / readtEXt / readCHUNK
unused_declarations.note: Display helpers: they build strings for the 010 Editor tree and write nothing to the file, so they carry no constraints of their own. readCHUNK is still the evidence for the bit-5 chunk-property semantics at lines 354-357.

PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[0].tier_rationale: The template prints '*ERROR: File is not a PNG image' and returns -1 (lines 371-372) if this word is not 0x8950; libpng rejects the file before reading any chunk.
PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[0].description: First signature word: bytes 0x89 'P' of the eight-byte PNG magic.
PNG_SIGNATURE.btPngSignature[0].notes: The .bt models the 8-byte PNG signature as four big-endian uint16 words (BigEndian() at line 39), so each word is pinned separately; the four compares at lines 367-370 are this template's front gate and libpng's equivalent is png_sig_cmp() over the first 8 bytes. Byte stream: 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A. The 0D 0A 1A 0A tail is what lets a decoder detect ASCII-mode corruption, so it is checked as literally as the %PNG head.

PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btRed.tier_rationale: A palette colour byte is never validated by a conforming decoder, and free colour values are what make one indexed image differ from the next inside the palette expansion code.
PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btRed.description: Red sample of one PLTE entry.
PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btRed.notes: Palette colour bytes are free: libpng copies them into its PLTE table and uses them in index-to-RGB expansion, tRNS alpha attachment and the bKGD/hIST/sPLT cross-checks. Varying them changes which gamma, sBIT-scaling and transparency branches run for a given index without risking the parse, so they stay completely free.

PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btGreen.tier_rationale: Free for the same reason as btRed: no decoder check, and green values drive the per-channel gamma and sBIT scaling paths independently.
PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btGreen.description: Green sample of one PLTE entry.
PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btGreen.notes: Palette colour bytes are free: libpng copies them into its PLTE table and uses them in index-to-RGB expansion, tRNS alpha attachment and the bKGD/hIST/sPLT cross-checks. Varying them changes which gamma, sBIT-scaling and transparency branches run for a given index without risking the parse, so they stay completely free.

PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btBlue.tier_rationale: Free for the same reason as btRed: no decoder check, and blue values exercise the same per-channel scaling code with different data.
PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btBlue.description: Blue sample of one PLTE entry.
PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btBlue.notes: Palette colour bytes are free: libpng copies them into its PLTE table and uses them in index-to-RGB expansion, tRNS alpha attachment and the bKGD/hIST/sPLT cross-checks. Varying them changes which gamma, sBIT-scaling and transparency branches run for a given index without risking the parse, so they stay completely free.

PNG_POINT.x.tier_rationale: A chromaticity coordinate is colour data the decoder does not gate on; pinning it to 'realistic' coordinates would remove colour-management variation and buy no depth.
PNG_POINT.x.description: X coordinate of one cHRM point, in 1/100000 units.
PNG_POINT.x.notes: cHRM stores chromaticities as unsigned 32-bit values scaled by 100000 (PNG 1.2 s.4.1.1). PNG_CHUNK_CHRM declares four PNG_POINT instances - white, red, green and blue at lines 157-160 - so the chunk's eight uint32 values are these two fields four times over, and per the innermost-typename rule the entries are keyed on PNG_POINT rather than on PNG_CHUNK_CHRM.white/red/green/blue. libpng stores the values and at most issues a benign warning for ones it cannot represent, so the file still decodes; these are colour values, which the tiering rules place in Tier C. The chunk's 32-byte extent is fixed by a dependency on CTYPE.cname, not by bounding these fields.

PNG_POINT.y.tier_rationale: Same as PNG_POINT.x: unvalidated colour data whose variation exercises the chromaticity-to-XYZ conversion arithmetic with different inputs.
PNG_POINT.y.description: Y coordinate of one cHRM point, in 1/100000 units.
PNG_POINT.y.notes: cHRM stores chromaticities as unsigned 32-bit values scaled by 100000 (PNG 1.2 s.4.1.1). PNG_CHUNK_CHRM declares four PNG_POINT instances - white, red, green and blue at lines 157-160 - so the chunk's eight uint32 values are these two fields four times over, and per the innermost-typename rule the entries are keyed on PNG_POINT rather than on PNG_CHUNK_CHRM.white/red/green/blue. libpng stores the values and at most issues a benign warning for ones it cannot represent, so the file still decodes; these are colour values, which the tiering rules place in Tier C. The chunk's 32-byte extent is fixed by a dependency on CTYPE.cname, not by bounding these fields.

CTYPE.cname.tier_rationale: These four bytes select which of the fifteen per-chunk structs the template instantiates (lines 301-330) and which libpng chunk handler runs; the legal set is every four-letter code with an uppercase third letter, so it is an enumeration to emit in full, not a value to pin.
CTYPE.cname.description: Four ASCII letters naming the chunk; bit 5 of each byte is a property flag and bit 5 of the third byte is reserved and must be 0, which is exactly why the third letter is uppercase.
CTYPE.cname.notes: Line 349 states the rule the pattern encodes ('Reserved bit: bit 5 of 3rd byte: MUST be 0') and line 356 labels a violation 'ERROR_RESERVED'. Lines 354-357 give the full bit-5 semantics: byte0 bit5 = ancillary(1)/critical(0), byte1 bit5 = private(1)/public(0), byte3 bit5 = safe-to-copy(1)/unsafe(0). The template uses no ReadUByte/ReadUShort lookahead anywhere: the type is parsed into this union and then compared against the fifteen literals at lines 301-330, so the set that matters to this parser is that literal list plus IDAT/IEND/gAMA/hIST/tRNS/iCCP/eXIf, which libpng knows but this .bt lets fall through to ubyte data[length]. Unrecognised four-letter codes are legal and are skipped after the CRC check, which is itself a libpng path worth visiting. valid_values is exhaustive over the registered chunk names but the pattern, not the list, is the true legal set. The only instance of this union in the file is PNG_CHUNK.type at line 300, so per the innermost-typename rule the entries are keyed on CTYPE rather than on PNG_CHUNK.type.

CTYPE.ctype.tier_rationale: Same four storage bytes as CTYPE.cname read as one big-endian uint32 (union at lines 112-115); whatever is legal for cname is legal here, so the full four-letter set must stay available rather than one pinned word.
CTYPE.ctype.description: The chunk type as a 32-bit big-endian word whose four bytes each spell an ASCII letter and whose third byte has bit 5 clear.
CTYPE.ctype.pattern: each of the four big-endian bytes is in [A-Za-z] and the third byte is in [A-Z]; e.g. 'IHDR' = 0x49484452, 'IDAT' = 0x49444154, 'IEND' = 0x49454E44
CTYPE.ctype.notes: Aliased with cname through the CTYPE union, so a generator writes the four letters once and both views are satisfied. Recorded separately because the .bt declares it as its own field and downstream tooling may key on either name.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.width.tier_rationale: Nothing in the format or in libpng restricts it beyond non-zero, and it is the primary driver of row-stride, unfilter and colour-expand work, so any bound here would delete the widest swath of decoder paths.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.width.description: Image width in pixels, big-endian uint32; it fixes the scanline byte count that the IDAT payload must supply.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.width.notes: This is the field the IDAT zlib stream must agree with, so the payload is derived from it and never the other way round: libpng allocates the row pointers and the pixel buffer from width x height x bytes-per-pixel and its unfilter loop runs height times (or the seven Adam7 pass heights when interlace_method is 1). Zero is the only value PNG 1.2 s.11.2.2 declares invalid for width and height and libpng refuses it ('Image width is zero in IHDR'), which is why excluded_values is recorded instead of any bound: every other uint32 is fair game and capping it to keep files small is exactly the mistake that costs coverage.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.height.tier_rationale: Free for the same reason as width: it is the row-loop bound, so narrowing it removes exactly the variation (few rows vs many rows, one row, tall and thin) that the de-interlacer and row-copy code respond to.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.height.description: Image height in pixels, big-endian uint32; it fixes how many filtered scanlines the IDAT payload must contain.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.height.notes: This is the field the IDAT zlib stream must agree with, so the payload is derived from it and never the other way round: libpng allocates the row pointers and the pixel buffer from width x height x bytes-per-pixel and its unfilter loop runs height times (or the seven Adam7 pass heights when interlace_method is 1). Zero is the only value PNG 1.2 s.11.2.2 declares invalid for width and height and libpng refuses it ('Image width is zero in IHDR'), which is why excluded_values is recorded instead of any bound: every other uint32 is fair game and capping it to keep files small is exactly the mistake that costs coverage.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.bits.tier_rationale: Bit depth is a finite enumeration and libpng refuses any value outside it ('Invalid bit depth for color type'), but five depths are legal and each takes a different sub-byte/byte/two-byte path through the unpacking code, so the whole set must be emitted.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.bits.description: Bits per sample (per channel, or per palette index for indexed colour); the legal subset depends on color_type.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.bits.notes: The union over all color types; per-color-type subsets are recorded as dependencies (indexed colour and grayscale allow 1/2/4, truecolour and alpha-bearing types allow only 8/16). Depths below 8 make libpng run its bit-unpacking and pixel-expansion code and forbid filter types 1-4 on the scanlines (also a dependency); depth 16 switches every sample to two bytes big-endian. All five must appear in the corpus.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type.tier_rationale: Five values are legal and each reconfigures the whole pixel pipeline (channels per pixel, palette lookup vs direct colour, alpha present or not); an illegal value makes libpng refuse the file, but the five legal ones are five distinct branch families and must all be emitted.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type.description: Colour model of the image, as declared by the pngColorSpaceType enum at lines 53-59.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.color_type.notes: Values 1, 5 and 7 are reserved by PNG 1.2 and libpng answers 'invalid color type'. color_type also decides the shape of bKGD (lines 195-217) and sBIT (lines 228-262), whether PLTE is mandatory or forbidden, how many samples per pixel the IDAT scanlines carry (1, 3, 1, 2, 4 for types 0, 2, 3, 4, 6) and which tRNS variant applies - all recorded as dependencies. Indexed (3) is the only value that forces the palette lookup path; AlphaTrueColor (6) is the deepest single-image path.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.compr_method.tier_rationale: A nonzero value makes libpng refuse the file with 'unknown compression method' before any pixel work, and the enum at lines 62-64 has exactly one member, so pinning it costs no diversity.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.compr_method.description: Compression method for the image data; PNG defines only deflate/inflate.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.compr_method.notes: Tier A rather than Tier B by the literal test: a wrong value stops the decoder outright because IHDR is a critical chunk. Recorded as enumerated_values rather than fixed_value because the .bt declares a typedef enum, so the enum checklist is satisfied and the single legal value is spelled out. Values 1-255 are undefined.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.filter_method.tier_rationale: A nonzero value makes libpng refuse the file with 'unknown filter method' before any row is unfiltered, and the enum at lines 67-69 has exactly one member.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.filter_method.description: Filter method applied to the scanlines inside the IDAT payload; PNG defines only adaptive filtering, whose five per-row filter types 0-4 live inside the payload.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.filter_method.notes: Same reasoning as compr_method. Do not confuse this method byte with the per-scanline filter-type byte inside the IDAT plaintext: that one takes 0-4 and is a diversity axis in its own right.

PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.interlace_method.tier_rationale: Both values are legal and they send the decoder down structurally different code: Adam7 reads seven passes with their own row offsets and strides, non-interlaced reads one pass. Any other value makes libpng refuse the file.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.interlace_method.description: Whether the pixel data is stored in one pass or in the seven interleaved Adam7 passes.
PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.interlace_method.notes: libpng answers 'unknown interlace method' for anything else. Adam7 changes the IDAT plaintext layout completely (seven sub-images whose dimensions are derived from width and height), so the payload must be derived from this field plus the dimensions - see the dependency. Both values must appear in the corpus: about half of libpng's interlace arithmetic is unreachable without method 1.

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.label.tier_rationale: Free-form Latin-1 keyword text; nothing but its NUL terminator is structural, and text content is the cheapest diversity in the file.
PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.label.description: tEXt keyword, read to the first NUL inclusive (comment on line 142).

evidence.snippet: string label;                              // to the first NULL (including)

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.label.notes: The extent of PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data on line 143 is derived as length - Strlen(label) - 1, so the label must contain exactly one NUL inside the chunk data or that extent goes negative. PNG 1.2 s.4.2.1 describes the keyword as 1-79 Latin-1 bytes with no leading or trailing spaces; libpng treats a malformed keyword as a benign error, so the field stays free and the NUL requirement is recorded as a dependency.

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data.tier_rationale: The text body is arbitrary bytes; constraining it removes free variation and buys no depth because libpng only copies it out.
PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data.description: tEXt text body: every remaining byte of the chunk after the NUL-terminated label.

evidence.snippet: char   data[length - Strlen(label) - 1];   // rest of the data

PNG_CHUNK_TEXT.data.notes: Its extent is computed by the template as length - Strlen(label) - 1, so the length is derived while the bytes inside it are free. Latin-1 by spec, unvalidated in practice.

PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.tier_rationale: libpng refuses a PLTE whose length is not a multiple of three ('invalid palette length') and refuses an indexed image whose palette is missing or smaller than the indices used, so the entry count is a derived value the decoder checks.
PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.description: The palette entry array: chunkLen/3 PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL elements, three bytes each.
PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.algorithm: element count = floor(PNG_CHUNK.length / 3), each element 3 bytes (btRed, btGreen, btBlue)
PNG_CHUNK_PLTE.plteChunkData.notes: The count is derived; the colours are not (PNG_PALETTE_PIXEL.btRed/btGreen/btBlue are Tier C). For color_type 3 the chunk is mandatory and PNG 1.2 s.3.3 caps it at 2^bit_depth entries; for color_type 0 and 4 a PLTE is forbidden, and for 2 and 6 it is an optional suggested palette (all recorded as dependencies). The entry count bounds the valid pixel indices inside the IDAT payload, so it belongs to the payload-derivation chain rather than to the free counts.

PNG_CHUNK_SRGB.srgbChunkData.tier_rationale: Four rendering intents are legal and libpng rejects anything else ('invalid sRGB data'); each intent selects a different colour-management path, so the whole set must be emittable.
PNG_CHUNK_SRGB.srgbChunkData.description: sRGB rendering intent, one byte, as declared by the enum at lines 88-93.
PNG_CHUNK_SRGB.srgbChunkData.notes: The chunk must be exactly one byte (dependency). Its presence also changes how libpng treats gAMA and cHRM, because it derives both from the sRGB profile - another branch worth visiting.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtIdChunkData.tier_rationale: Free-form UTF-8 keyword; nothing in the decoder gates on its content and free text is cheap diversity.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtIdChunkData.notes: The extent of itxtValChunkData (lines 173-177) is derived by subtracting the lengths of this keyword, the language tag and the translated keyword plus their three NULs and the two flag/method bytes, so each of those strings must be NUL-terminated inside the chunk.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtCompressionFlag.tier_rationale: Two values are legal and they send the value bytes down completely different code (plain UTF-8 copy vs zlib inflate); libpng reports a benign error for anything else, so the whole set must be emitted.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtCompressionFlag.description: Whether the iTXt text that follows the language tag and translated keyword is zlib-compressed.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtCompressionFlag.notes: libpng answers 'invalid iTXt compression flag' (benign error, chunk dropped) for values above 1. Value 1 is the interesting one: it makes an ancillary text chunk run the same inflate machinery as IDAT, and the payload shape is recorded as a dependency so the text bytes stay free inside a well-formed zlib stream.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtComprMethod.tier_rationale: Only deflate is defined, but this sits in an ancillary chunk: libpng reports 'unknown compression method' as a benign error and skips the chunk instead of refusing the file, so by the literal Tier A test it is Tier B.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtComprMethod.description: Compression method for the iTXt text, as declared by PNG_COMPR_METHOD (lines 62-64).
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtComprMethod.notes: Emit 0 so the chunk is actually parsed; the tier records that a wrong value costs this chunk, not the file. Contrast PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.compr_method, which is Tier A because IHDR is critical.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtLanguageTag.tier_rationale: A free-form RFC 3066 language tag terminated by NUL; the decoder stores it without validation, so any bound here would cost diversity for nothing.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtLanguageTag.description: iTXt language tag, NUL-terminated (may be empty).
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtLanguageTag.notes: Must contain a NUL inside the chunk because itxtValChunkData's extent on lines 173-177 subtracts Strlen(itxtLanguageTag) + 1.

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtTranslatedKeyword.tier_rationale: Free-form UTF-8 text, NUL-terminated and not validated; constraining it removes variation without adding depth.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtTranslatedKeyword.description: iTXt translated keyword, NUL-terminated (may be empty).
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtTranslatedKeyword.notes: Must contain a NUL inside the chunk for the same derived-extent reason as the language tag (lines 173-177).

PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.tier_rationale: The text body is free bytes when the compression flag is 0, and free bytes *inside* a well-formed zlib stream when it is 1; either way the field itself carries no value set.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.description: iTXt text: the rest of the chunk after keyword, flags, language tag and translated keyword.
PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtValChunkData.notes: Extent is derived by the arithmetic on lines 173-177. When PNG_CHUNK_ITXT.itxtCompressionFlag is 1 these bytes must be a zlib stream (recorded as a dependency pointing at the same construction as zTXt); when it is 0 they are plain UTF-8. This is the one field where a Tier C declaration and a Tier A payload rule coexist, and the dependency is what resolves it.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtIdChunkData.tier_rationale: Free-form Latin-1 keyword, NUL-terminated; unvalidated content whose variation is free diversity.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtIdChunkData.notes: The extent of ztxtValChunkData on line 183 is chunkLen - Strlen(ztxtIdChunkData) - 2, so the keyword must carry exactly one NUL inside the chunk.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.comprMethod.tier_rationale: Only deflate is defined, but like the iTXt case this is an ancillary chunk: libpng issues a benign 'unknown compression method' error and drops the chunk rather than refusing the file.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.comprMethod.description: Compression method for the zTXt text, as declared by PNG_COMPR_METHOD (lines 62-64).
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.comprMethod.notes: Emit 0 so the compressed text is actually inflated and the chunk's code runs.

PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.tier_rationale: These bytes are the compressed text; if they are not a zlib stream libpng's inflate fails and the chunk is dropped before any text handling runs, so the parse never reaches the code this chunk exists to exercise.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.description: zTXt compressed text: a zlib stream whose payload is the Latin-1 text body.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.must_produce: a complete zlib stream: a CMF byte with CM=8 and CINFO<=7 (0x78 for the 32 KiB window), a FLG byte with FDICT=0 and FCHECK chosen so (CMF*256 + FLG) % 31 == 0 (0x78 0x01 and 0x78 0x9C both work), one or more deflate blocks whose last block sets BFINAL=1, and a trailing 4-byte big-endian Adler-32 of the uncompressed bytes, wrapping the uncompressed Latin-1 text bytes
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.decoder_gate: libpng routes zTXt through png_inflate; a non-zlib byte run fails with 'zTXt: inflate error' / benign error 'invalid compressed text buffer' and the chunk is discarded, so neither the inflate loop nor the text callback runs
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.generation_strategy: Build deflate *stored* blocks - no Huffman tables, no window search. Per block: align to a byte boundary, write one byte whose low 3 bits are BFINAL|BTYPE<<1 (0x00 = non-final stored, 0x01 = final stored), then LEN as a little-endian uint16 of at most 65535, then NLEN = ~LEN as a little-endian uint16, then LEN literal bytes. Repeat until the plaintext is consumed and the last block is marked final, then append the Adler-32 of the whole plaintext, big-endian. Prefix the two zlib header bytes 0x78 0x01. This is valid, trivial to emit, and takes the decoder all the way through inflate. The plaintext is arbitrary text, so choose the text first and wrap it; nothing about the text is constrained.
PNG_CHUNK_ZTXT.ztxtValChunkData.notes: The template derives this field's extent as chunkLen - Strlen(ztxtIdChunkData) - 2 (line 183), so PNG_CHUNK.length must be set from the finished zlib byte count - derive the stream, then the length, never the reverse. This is the second-cheapest place in the file to exercise zlib after IDAT.

PNG_CHUNK_SBIT.sbitRed.tier_rationale: A significant-bits count looks like a bit depth and invites a value set, but no conforming decoder refuses the file over it (libpng reports it benignly and drops only the chunk), so pinning it would delete the sample-scaling variation it feeds.
PNG_CHUNK_SBIT.sbitRed.description: sBIT significant-bit count for the indexed colour (color_type 3) shape of the chunk.
PNG_CHUNK_SBIT.sbitRed.notes: sBIT records how many bits of each sample are significant. The struct is a switch on IHDR.color_type (lines 228-262), so which of these fields exists at all is decided by that field (dependencies). PNG 1.2 s.4.2.2 requires each value to be at least 1 and at most the sample depth (8 for indexed colour, IHDR.bits otherwise), and libpng reports 'invalid sBIT data' as a benign error when the rule is broken, dropping only the chunk. The bound is therefore recorded as a dependency - a format rule - and the field itself stays free, because scaling samples by differing significant-bit counts is exactly the variation that drives libpng's sample-scaling code.

PNG_CHUNK_ACTL.num_frames.covers: n/a: a declared count of chunks, not a byte extent
PNG_CHUNK_ACTL.num_frames.notes: acTL is 8 bytes (dependency) and must appear before the first fcTL and before the first IDAT. Because the count is derived from the chunks the generator decides to emit, the frame count stays a free choice: pick how many frames you want, emit that many fcTL chunks, then write the number here.

PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data.tier_rationale: These bytes are the frame's compressed pixels; if they are not a decodable zlib stream libpng's inflate fails, the frame is dropped and none of the per-frame unfilter, composite or dispose code runs.
PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data.description: APNG frame image data: the frame's zlib-compressed filtered scanlines, spread over the consecutive fdAT chunks belonging to that frame.
PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data.must_produce: a complete zlib stream: a CMF byte with CM=8 and CINFO<=7 (0x78 for the 32 KiB window), a FLG byte with FDICT=0 and FCHECK chosen so (CMF*256 + FLG) % 31 == 0 (0x78 0x01 and 0x78 0x9C both work), one or more deflate blocks whose last block sets BFINAL=1, and a trailing 4-byte big-endian Adler-32 of the uncompressed bytes, where the plaintext is the frame's filtered scanlines: for each of PNG_CHUNK_FCTL.height rows one filter-type byte (0-4) followed by ceil(frame_width * samples_per_pixel * bits / 8) bytes, with samples_per_pixel taken from IHDR.color_type (1, 3, 1, 2, 4 for types 0, 2, 3, 4, 6) and seven interleaved passes instead of one row run when IHDR.interlace_method is 1. Concatenating this frame's fdAT payloads in order must yield exactly that one stream.
PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data.decoder_gate: libpng's APNG support inflates fdAT payloads into the frame buffer; random bytes fail with 'fdAT: inflate error' / 'invalid fdAT length' and the frame is discarded, so png_read_filter_row and the composite/dispose code for that frame never execute
PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data.generation_strategy: Build deflate *stored* blocks - no Huffman tables, no window search. Per block: align to a byte boundary, write one byte whose low 3 bits are BFINAL|BTYPE<<1 (0x00 = non-final stored, 0x01 = final stored), then LEN as a little-endian uint16 of at most 65535, then NLEN = ~LEN as a little-endian uint16, then LEN literal bytes. Repeat until the plaintext is consumed and the last block is marked final, then append the Adler-32 of the whole plaintext, big-endian. Prefix the two zlib header bytes 0x78 0x01. This is valid, trivial to emit, and takes the decoder all the way through inflate. Build the frame plaintext from the fcTL geometry and the IHDR pixel format first, then wrap it; the filtered bytes inside are free, so random or patterned pixel data costs nothing. Split the resulting stream across as many fdAT chunks as the output budget wants, with each chunk's length = 4 + its slice size.
PNG_CHUNK_FDAT.frame_data.notes: Frame-independence caveat: libpng's APNG implementation re-initialises its inflate state at the start of each frame, so the safest construction is one complete zlib stream per frame (frame 0's stream living in the IDAT chain and each later frame's stream living in its own fdAT chain). Some descriptions of APNG instead treat IDAT+fdAT as a single continuous stream; if the target decoder is known to expect that, continue the deflate block sequence across frames without a second zlib header and emit the Adler-32 only at the very end. Both readings agree that the frame's payload size is derived from the fcTL geometry - never shrink the geometry to fit a precomputed payload.

PNG_CHUNK.length.tier_rationale: Every per-chunk array extent in the template is computed from it (lines 143, 153, 173-177, 183, 267, 289) and libpng refuses a chunk whose declared length disagrees with the bytes that chunk type consumes ('invalid IHDR length', 'invalid palette length'), so the decode stops at that chunk.

PNG_CHUNK.length.algorithm: byte count of the chunk data field; the template measures it as data_size = FTell() - pos_start (line 333) with pos_start taken right after length (line 299)
PNG_CHUNK.length.covers: the bytes between the end of CTYPE.type and the start of PNG_CHUNK.crc, i.e. pos_start through pos_start + length; for a dispatched chunk type that is the parsed per-chunk struct, for anything else it is ubyte data[length] (line 332)
PNG_CHUNK.length.notes: Per-type lengths the spec fixes and libpng enforces: IHDR 13, IEND 0, cHRM 32, sRGB 1, gAMA 4, tIME 7, pHYs 9, acTL 8, fcTL 26, PLTE a multiple of 3, hIST 2 x the palette entry count, IDAT arbitrary but the whole IDAT chain must form one zlib stream. Each of those is recorded as a dependency so that `length` itself stays a derived value for free-form chunk types (tEXt, zTXt, iTXt, sPLT, unknown). This is a length prefix in the GIF sense: it counts only the payload that follows the type field.

PNG_CHUNK.data.tier_rationale: For an IDAT chunk these bytes are the compressed image: random bytes make libpng fail inside png_inflate and abort the row pipeline, so the file is rejected after the header and almost nothing below the chunk dispatcher executes.
PNG_CHUNK.data.description: The chunk data for every type the template does not dispatch on (lines 301-330) - which includes IDAT, IEND, gAMA, hIST, tRNS, iCCP, eXIf and all unknown chunks. For IDAT it is a slice of the one zlib stream that carries the whole image.
PNG_CHUNK.data.codec: zlib/deflate (RFC 1950 zlib wrapper + RFC 1951 deflate) for IDAT; unconstrained bytes for every other chunk type that reaches this field
PNG_CHUNK.data.must_produce: Concatenating the data of all IDAT chunks in file order must yield exactly a complete zlib stream: a CMF byte with CM=8 and CINFO<=7 (0x78 for the 32 KiB window), a FLG byte with FDICT=0 and FCHECK chosen so (CMF*256 + FLG) % 31 == 0 (0x78 0x01 and 0x78 0x9C both work), one or more deflate blocks whose last block sets BFINAL=1, and a trailing 4-byte big-endian Adler-32 of the uncompressed bytes. Its plaintext is the filtered scanline data: for each row one filter-type byte in 0-4 followed by ceil(width * samples_per_pixel * bits / 8) bytes, where samples_per_pixel is 1, 3, 1, 2, 4 for color_type 0, 2, 3, 4, 6 respectively, rows are emitted top to bottom, and when interlace_method is 1 the rows of the seven Adam7 passes replace that single run (pass dimensions derived from width and height). Each IDAT chunk's PNG_CHUNK.length is the size of its own slice.
PNG_CHUNK.data.decoder_gate: libpng inflates the IDAT chain into its row buffers; a non-zlib byte run fails immediately with 'IDAT: invalid block type', 'invalid window size', 'IDAT: incorrect data check' (Adler-32 mismatch) or 'not enough image data', and png_read_finish_row / png_read_filter_row / the palette, gamma, sBIT and alpha pipelines never run. Getting this right is what moves the decoder from the chunk dispatcher into the pixel code - the single highest-value entry in this file.
PNG_CHUNK.data.generation_strategy: Derive the plaintext from the header, never the reverse. (1) Compute samples_per_pixel from color_type (1, 3, 1, 2, 4 for types 0, 2, 3, 4, 6) and row_bytes = ceil(width * samples_per_pixel * bits / 8); for interlace_method 0 the plaintext total is height * (row_bytes + 1). For Adam7 replace that single run with seven passes, pass p using pass_width = ceil((width - xstart[p]) / xstep[p]) and pass_height = ceil((height - ystart[p]) / ystep[p]) with the xstart/ystart/xstep/ystep table given in the interlace dependency, and its own row_bytes per pass. (2) Fill each row with one filter-type byte (0, or 0-4 when bits >= 8) followed by row_bytes arbitrary bytes - the pixel content is free. (3) Wrap that plaintext with Build deflate *stored* blocks - no Huffman tables, no window search. Per block: align to a byte boundary, write one byte whose low 3 bits are BFINAL|BTYPE<<1 (0x00 = non-final stored, 0x01 = final stored), then LEN as a little-endian uint16 of at most 65535, then NLEN = ~LEN as a little-endian uint16, then LEN literal bytes. Repeat until the plaintext is consumed and the last block is marked final, then append the Adler-32 of the whole plaintext, big-endian. Prefix the two zlib header bytes 0x78 0x01. This is valid, trivial to emit, and takes the decoder all the way through inflate. (4) Split the zlib byte run across one or more consecutive IDAT chunks, set each chunk's length to its slice size and its CRC over type+slice. Emitting several IDAT chunks instead of one is free diversity inside a correct stream.
PNG_CHUNK.data.notes: The .bt gives no hint of any of this: IDAT is absent from the dispatch chain at lines 301-330 and lands in this generic array, so the payload rule comes entirely from the format. Two consequences matter for generation. First, for chunk types that genuinely carry opaque data - unknown private chunks, gAMA (4 bytes), tRNS (2, 6 or one byte per palette entry), hIST (2 bytes per palette entry), eXIf - the bytes are free and only their extent is derived; the dependency section records which types need what, including iCCP, whose data after name+NUL+method must itself be a zlib stream. Second, all IDAT chunks must be consecutive and the chain must hold exactly the number of plaintext bytes the header implies: too few gives 'not enough image data', too many gives 'extra compressed data', both benign-to-fatal in libpng. The filter-type byte inside the plaintext is the cheapest deep diversity in the format: five filter types times every row.

PNG_CHUNK.crc.tier_rationale: A wrong CRC makes this template print '*ERROR: CRC Mismatch @ chunk[%d]' (line 338) and makes libpng raise 'CRC error', which is fatal for a critical chunk: the decode stops at that chunk and nothing after it runs.
PNG_CHUNK.crc.description: CRC-32 of the chunk's type and data bytes, stored big-endian.

evidence.snippet: local uint32 crc_calc = Checksum(CHECKSUM_CRC32, pos_start, data_size);

PNG_CHUNK.crc.algorithm: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC as used by PNG (poly 0x04C11DB7 normal / 0xEDB88320 reflected, init 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF); the template computes it with Checksum(CHECKSUM_CRC32, pos_start, data_size)
PNG_CHUNK.crc.covers: the 4 chunk-type bytes followed by the `length` data bytes: pos_start is FTell() taken immediately after PNG_CHUNK.length (line 299) and data_size is FTell() - pos_start measured after the per-chunk struct or data array has been read (line 333). The 4 length bytes are excluded, as the comment on line 36 says ('CRC Does NOT include the length bytes'), and so is the CRC field itself.

PNG_CHUNK.crc.notes: Compute it last, over the bytes actually written, so it stays correct when the chunk type, the length or the payload was derived from something else. For ancillary chunks libpng treats a CRC failure as a benign error and skips the chunk, which is still a lost path; for IHDR/PLTE/IDAT/IEND it ends the file. IEND's CRC is over the four type bytes only (0xAE426082) because its length is 0.
