dependencies.description: Adam7 interlacing replaces the single top-to-bottom row run with seven sub-image runs, so the IDAT plaintext layout is derived from interlace_method together with the dimensions.
dependencies.notes: Adam7 xstart 0,4,0,2,0,1,0; ystart 0,0,4,0,2,0,1; xstep 8,8,4,4,2,2,1; ystep 8,8,8,4,4,2,2. Getting the total byte count right is what keeps libpng from reporting 'not enough image data'.

then.pattern: every per-row filter-type byte inside the IDAT plaintext must be 0

dependencies.description: At bit depths below 8 only filter type 0 (None) is permitted on a scanline, because the other four filters operate on whole bytes.
dependencies.notes: PNG 1.2 s.6.2.2 and s.9.3: filter types 1-4 are not used for bit depths under 8; libpng reports 'invalid filter type' for anything above 4 regardless of depth. The row content bytes stay free.

then.pattern: x_offset + width <= PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.width and y_offset + height <= PNG_CHUNK_IHDR.height, with width and height non-zero

dependencies.description: A frame region must fit inside the IHDR canvas.
dependencies.notes: A format rule relating four Tier C fields to two others; the fields themselves stay free and the frame's fdAT payload is derived from them.

then.algorithm: number of fcTL chunks in the file

dependencies.description: acTL.num_frames must equal the number of fcTL chunks actually present.

then.position: before the first fcTL and before the first IDAT

dependencies.description: APNG frame chunks are only meaningful when an acTL chunk precedes them; without it libpng treats fcTL and fdAT as unknown chunks and no animation code runs.
dependencies.notes: Frame 0's fcTL may appear before the first IDAT (frame 0 is then part of the animation) or the first IDAT may stand alone with fcTL starting at frame 1.

then.algorithm: length = 4 (sequence_number) + the size of this chunk's slice of the frame's zlib stream
then.covers: the fdAT data field, whose first 4 bytes are the sequence number

dependencies.description: The fdAT data field is a 4-byte sequence number followed by frame data, which is why the template reads frame_data[length-4] on line 289.
The sPLT entry area must be a whole number of entries: 6 bytes per entry at sample depth 8, 10 bytes per entry at sample depth 16.
dependencies.notes: libpng reports 'invalid sPLT length' benignly otherwise. The entry bytes themselves stay free.

then.pattern: exactly one NUL byte inside the chunk data, terminating the keyword

dependencies.description: The tEXt keyword must be NUL-terminated inside the chunk because the template derives the following field's extent from Strlen().
dependencies.notes: The string content stays free; only the terminator is structural.

then.pattern: exactly one NUL byte inside the chunk data, terminating the keyword

dependencies.description: The zTXt keyword must be NUL-terminated inside the chunk because the template derives the following field's extent from Strlen().
dependencies.notes: The string content stays free; only the terminator is structural.

then.pattern: exactly one NUL byte inside the chunk data, terminating the keyword

dependencies.description: The iTXt keyword must be NUL-terminated inside the chunk because the template derives the following field's extent from Strlen().
dependencies.notes: The string content stays free; only the terminator is structural.

then.pattern: exactly one NUL byte inside the chunk data, terminating the palette name

dependencies.description: The sPLT palette name must be NUL-terminated inside the chunk because the template derives the following field's extent from Strlen().
dependencies.notes: The string content stays free; only the terminator is structural.

dependencies.description: An indexed-colour background must name an existing palette entry.
dependencies.notes: libpng warns benignly when the index is out of palette bounds, so this is a derived relation rather than a bound on the byte.

structure.subject: PNG_SIGNATURE
structure.detail: The eight signature bytes 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A are the first bytes of the file; the template instantiates PNG_SIGNATURE before the chunk loop (line 365) and returns -1 if the four uint16 words do not match (lines 367-373).
structure.description: A PNG file starts with a fixed 8-byte signature and nothing may precede it.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed 8-byte head element, then the chunk array.
structure.notes: libpng's png_sig_cmp refuses the file at this point; there is no recovery.

structure.subject: chunk type "IHDR"
structure.detail: IHDR must be the first chunk; the template checks chunk[0].type.cname != "IHDR" and prints '*ERROR: Chunk IHDR must be first chunk.' (lines 381-384).
structure.description: The image header is the first chunk of the series.
structure.generation_note: emit IHDR immediately after the signature, exactly once.
structure.notes: The template's guard only fires when CHUNK_CNT > 1 (line 381), so a single-chunk file escapes the check in 010 Editor; libpng applies it unconditionally.

structure.subject: chunk type "IEND"
structure.detail: IEND must be the last chunk; the template checks chunk[CHUNK_CNT-1].type.cname != "IEND" and prints '*ERROR: Chunk IEND must be last chunk.' (lines 385-387).
structure.description: The chunk series is terminated by IEND.
structure.generation_note: emit IEND as a fixed 12-byte tail: length 0x00000000, type 'IEND', no data, CRC 0xAE426082.

structure.subject: any bytes after the IEND chunk
structure.detail: The chunk loop runs while(!FEof()) (line 376), so trailing bytes are parsed as further chunks and libpng reports 'chunk after IEND'; nothing may follow the terminator.
structure.description: The file ends with the last byte of IEND's CRC.
structure.generation_note: write no padding, no alignment bytes and no trailing newline after IEND.

structure.subject: PNG_CHUNK series
structure.detail: Chunks are packed back to back with no padding, alignment or separators: the template reads length, type, data, crc and immediately loops for the next chunk (lines 376-379).
structure.description: The chunk series is a dense sequence of length|type|data|crc records.
structure.output_budget: Total file budget: 1 MiB (1048576 bytes) by default, held as a running total of bytes already written and checked before each chunk is emitted; stop adding optional chunks when the next one would not fit. Mandatory overhead is tiny and always fits: signature 8 B, IHDR 25 B (12 B envelope + 13 B data), IEND 12 B. This is the only size control in the document: no field is capped to achieve it. If the derived IDAT payload for the chosen dimensions would exceed the remaining budget, redraw the dimensions and derive again - never shrink the dimensions to a fixed small set so that a precomputed payload fits.
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed head (signature + IHDR), then a repeated array of optional chunks bounded by output_budget, then the fixed tail (IEND). Each chunk costs 12 bytes of envelope plus its data.

structure.subject: PNG_CHUNK.length
structure.detail: Every chunk carries its own data length as its first 4 bytes, counting only the data field (comment at line 298 and the format summary at lines 34-36).
structure.description: The chunk envelope is self-describing: length, type, data, CRC.
structure.generation_note: build each chunk's data first, then write its byte count, the type, the data, and the CRC over type+data.

structure.subject: chunk type "IHDR"
structure.detail: Exactly one IHDR chunk must be present; it carries the only copy of width, height, bits, color_type and the three method bytes that every other rule depends on.

structure.subject: chunk type "IHDR"
structure.detail: At most one IHDR; libpng reports 'duplicate IHDR' for a second one and stops reading header fields.

structure.subject: chunk type "IDAT"
structure.detail: At least one IDAT chunk must be present: with no pixel data libpng errors ('No IDAT chunks') and no row processing happens.
structure.description: The image data chain is mandatory.
structure.generation_note: emit one or more IDAT chunks after the palette and colour-space chunks.

structure.subject: IDAT chunk chain
structure.detail: All IDAT chunks must be consecutive; PNG 1.2 s.5.3 requires the image data to be contiguous in the chunk series and libpng reports 'IDAT: out of place' when another chunk type is interleaved.
structure.description: The IDAT chain is one unbroken run of chunks that together form a single zlib stream.
structure.output_budget: Charged from the same 1 MiB running total; the default share for the compressed pixel data is up to 512 KiB. The uncompressed plaintext size is already fixed by the header (height * (row_bytes + 1), or the seven-pass total when interlaced), so the budget is met by choosing dimensions whose derived plaintext fits - deflate stored blocks add only 5 bytes per 65535 bytes of plaintext.
structure.generation_note: Build the whole zlib byte run first, then slice it across N consecutive IDAT chunks (N >= 1) chosen freely; each slice gets its own length and CRC. Varying N is free structural diversity.

structure.subject: chunk type "PLTE"
structure.detail: PLTE must appear before the first IDAT; it is mandatory when color_type is 3 and forbidden when color_type is 0 or 4.
structure.condition: mandatory for color_type 3, optional for 2 and 6, forbidden for 0 and 4
structure.description: The palette precedes the pixel data that indexes into it.
structure.generation_note: emit PLTE after the colour-space chunks and before the IDAT chain.

structure.subject: chunk types "gAMA", "cHRM", "sRGB", "iCCP", "sBIT"
structure.detail: Colour-space and significant-bits chunks must appear before PLTE and before the first IDAT (PNG 1.2 Table 5.3).
structure.description: Colour description precedes both the palette and the pixels.
structure.generation_note: emit these in the block between IHDR and PLTE.

structure.subject: chunk types "tRNS", "bKGD", "hIST", "pHYs"
structure.detail: tRNS, bKGD and hIST must appear after PLTE when a palette exists and before the first IDAT; pHYs must also precede the first IDAT (PNG 1.2 Table 5.3).
structure.description: Palette-dependent ancillary chunks sit between PLTE and IDAT.
structure.generation_note: emit after PLTE, before the IDAT chain.

structure.subject: PNG_CHUNK_BKGD and PNG_CHUNK_SBIT switch arms
structure.detail: Both struct bodies are switches on IHDR.color_type (lines 195-217 and 228-262), so only one arm's fields exist in a given file: indexed, grayscale, grayscale+alpha, truecolour, truecolour+alpha.
structure.description: Exactly one bKGD shape and one sBIT shape per file, chosen by color_type.
structure.generation_note: select the arm from color_type, emit those bytes, then set PNG_CHUNK.length from the byte count.

structure.subject: ancillary chunks "bKGD", "cHRM", "gAMA", "hIST", "iCCP", "pHYs", "sBIT", "sRGB", "tIME", "tRNS"
structure.detail: At most one of each of these types; a duplicate makes libpng report 'duplicate <type>' as a benign error and ignore the extra copy.
structure.generation_note: pick a random subset of them per file; the subset choice is itself diversity and costs no field narrowing.

structure.subject: chunk types "tEXt", "zTXt", "iTXt", "sPLT"
structure.detail: Any number of text and suggested-palette chunks may appear anywhere between IHDR and IEND, and repeating them is legal.
structure.description: Text and sPLT chunks repeat freely.
structure.output_budget: 4 KiB total across all text and sPLT chunks in one file, charged to the same 1 MiB running total; stop adding text chunks when the next one would not fit. Keyword and body byte counts are free within that budget and carry no other bound.
structure.generation_note: emit a budget-bounded array of text chunks with random keywords and bodies; size sPLT entries from sampleDepth.

structure.subject: unknown chunk types (CTYPE.cname outside the registered set)
structure.detail: Any number of unrecognised chunks may appear between IHDR and IEND; the template reads them as ubyte data[length] (lines 331-332) and libpng skips them after the CRC check, honouring the safe-to-copy bit.
structure.description: Unknown chunks are legal and repeatable.
structure.output_budget: 1 KiB total across unknown chunks in one file, charged to the same running total; each unknown chunk still costs 12 bytes of envelope.
structure.generation_note: invent four-letter names with an uppercase third letter and bit 5 set in the first two bytes (ancillary, private) so they read as well-formed unknown chunks; their data bytes are free.

structure.subject: chunk type "acTL"
structure.detail: acTL must precede the first fcTL and the first IDAT for the file to be treated as APNG.
structure.condition: only when fcTL or fdAT chunks are present
structure.description: The animation control chunk opens the APNG section.
structure.generation_note: emit acTL immediately after IHDR when generating an animation.

structure.subject: chunk types "fcTL" and "fdAT"
structure.detail: One fcTL per frame, followed by that frame's IDAT (frame 0) or fdAT (later frames) chunks; the fcTL count must equal acTL.num_frames and the shared sequence counter must increase across both chunk types.
structure.description: Frame chunks repeat once per animation frame.
structure.output_budget: Frames are charged to the same 1 MiB running total: each frame costs 38 bytes of envelope (fcTL 26 + 12, plus 12 per fdAT) plus its derived compressed pixel data, and all frame data together shares the 512 KiB pixel-data share. Choose the frame count and each frame's geometry first, derive the payloads from them, and stop adding frames when the budget is exhausted - never fix the frame geometry to a small set so a precomputed payload fits.
structure.generation_note: emit acTL(num_frames=N), then for each frame an fcTL with derived geometry followed by that frame's IDAT or fdAT chain.

diversity_axes.name: png_signature
diversity_axes.why: Listed so the rewrite step sees the pin explicitly and does not try to 'diversify' the magic: this is the one field in the file that must never vary.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A wrong word ends the parse at the signature check, so there is no decoder path to explore here at all.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Never: emit 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A on every file.
diversity_axes.notes: An axis with must_remain_unconstrained false is a protection note, not a freedom note.

diversity_axes.name: chunk_length
diversity_axes.why: Derived, not chosen: it varies because the chunk mix, the palette size, the text lengths and the IDAT slicing vary. Capping it would silently truncate payloads.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng branches on the declared length of every chunk type (fixed-length checks, multiple-of-3 palette checks, the inflate byte budget), so different lengths reach different validation branches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Compute from the bytes actually emitted for that chunk. Values span the whole uint32 space in principle because unknown-chunk data length is free; in practice it follows the output budget.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: No separate budget: chunk lengths are what the 1 MiB running total is charged against.
diversity_axes.notes: Never invent a length and then emit that many bytes of something else: build the chunk data, then measure it.

diversity_axes.name: chunk_type_name
diversity_axes.why: The single biggest driver of which code runs: each chunk name selects a different libpng handler, and the presence/absence of an ancillary chunk enables whole subsystems (palette, gamma, sRGB, transparency, physical scale, text, ICC profile, animation).
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Every registered chunk type is a separate function in libpng plus its validation branches; unknown types take the skip-and-safe-to-copy path. Bit-5 combinations add the ancillary/private/critical classification branches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw a different random subset of the registered chunk names per file, plus occasionally an invented ancillary-private name; always include IHDR first, at least one IDAT, and IEND last. Cover all five color_type/bits combinations across the corpus so the conditional chunks appear in the files where they are legal.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Bounded only by the 4 KiB text share, the 1 KiB unknown-chunk share and the singleton rule on the non-repeatable ancillary types.
diversity_axes.notes: Do not drop the awkward types (iCCP with its profile inflate, sPLT with its two sample depths, hIST, eXIf) - they are distinct handlers.

diversity_axes.name: chunk_crc
diversity_axes.why: Derived from the bytes actually written; varying it independently would be an error, not diversity.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A correct CRC keeps the decoder in the chunk; a wrong one ends a critical chunk's parse. Ancillary chunks with bad CRCs take the benign-error skip path, which is reachable only by getting the rest of the file right first.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Never varies for a given chunk content: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC over type+data, big-endian.
diversity_axes.notes: Compute last, after the payload was derived.

diversity_axes.name: idat_zlib_stream
diversity_axes.why: This is where depth lives: the pixels. Its envelope is pinned (zlib) but its contents - the filter-type byte per row, the pixel bytes, how many IDAT chunks the stream is split across - are free, so it is simultaneously the deepest and one of the most diverse parts of the file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng's inflate loop, the five per-row unfilter routines (None/Sub/Up/Average/Paeth), sub-byte unpacking at depths 1/2/4, 16-bit big-endian sample handling, palette index expansion, alpha compositing, gamma and sBIT scaling, and the seven-pass Adam7 row interleave all live behind a well-formed zlib stream.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Derive the plaintext size from the header, then vary freely inside it: filter type per row (0 always, 1-4 when bits >= 8), pixel byte content, number of IDAT chunks the stream is split across, and the deflate block style (stored blocks always work; fixed-Huffman blocks are also cheap and take zlib through a different inflate branch).
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Up to 512 KiB of the 1 MiB file budget; the uncompressed size is fixed by the header, so the budget is met by choosing dimensions first and deriving, never by shrinking dimensions to fit a fixed payload.
diversity_axes.notes: content_is_free true is the whole trick: pin the envelope, free the contents.

diversity_axes.name: palette_entry_count
diversity_axes.why: The entry count is derived from the chunk length and bounds the legal pixel indices, so it varies with the palette the generator decides to emit; the colours inside are free and are their own axis.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng builds its palette table from the entry count, validates tRNS/hIST/bKGD against it, and expands indexed pixels through it - a palette of 2 entries and a palette of 256 entries exercise different bounds checks and different index distributions.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose any entry count from 1 up to 2^bits (and up to the output budget), then set PLTE length = 3 * count and derive the index bytes in the IDAT plaintext from that count.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Charged to the 1 MiB total; at 3 bytes per entry even a 256-entry palette is 768 bytes, so the palette is never the reason to shrink anything else.
diversity_axes.notes: Derive the pixel indices from the palette size, never the palette size from a fixed index table.

diversity_axes.name: ztxt_zlib_stream
diversity_axes.why: A second, cheap place to exercise the inflate machinery; its envelope is pinned and the text inside is free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng inflates zTXt through the same png_inflate path as IDAT and then runs its text callback, so a correct stream reaches code a tEXt chunk never touches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Random uncompressed text, random stored-block slicing, random keyword; set the chunk length from the finished stream.
diversity_axes.notes: Same construction as IDAT minus the scanline structure.

diversity_axes.name: fdat_zlib_continuation
diversity_axes.why: Per-frame pixel data for APNG: derived from the fcTL geometry, free inside the stream.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each frame runs the unfilter and composite path again with its own dimensions and its own dispose/blend combination; frames that differ in size reach different blit bounds.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Derive each frame's plaintext from its fcTL geometry, vary the filter types and pixel bytes, and split across as many fdAT chunks as you like.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Shares the 512 KiB pixel-data budget across all frames.
diversity_axes.notes: See the frame-independence caveat on the constraint entry.

diversity_axes.name: apng_sequence_counter
diversity_axes.why: A running counter shared with fdAT; it varies automatically with the number and order of frame chunks.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng's APNG code compares it against its expected next value, so a correct counter is what keeps the frame loop running instead of dropping frames.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 0, 1, 2, ... across fcTL and fdAT in file order.
diversity_axes.notes: Never reset per frame.

diversity_axes.name: apng_sequence_counter_fdat
diversity_axes.why: Same shared counter as fcTL, incremented on every fdAT chunk as well.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Out-of-order counters make libpng drop the frame data, losing the whole per-frame pipeline.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Continue the file-wide counter; a frame split over several fdAT chunks increments on each of them.
diversity_axes.notes: The counter occupies the first 4 bytes of the fdAT data field, which is why frame_data's extent is length-4.

diversity_axes.name: apng_frame_count
diversity_axes.why: Derived from how many fcTL chunks the generator chose to emit; the choice of frame count is free and is what makes animations differ.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A mismatch makes libpng's APNG support drop the animation; a correct count lets the frame loop run to completion, and more frames mean more passes through the compositing code.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Pick the frame count first (the budget decides how many fit), emit that many fcTL chunks, then write the count here.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Each frame costs 38 bytes of envelope plus its derived pixel data inside the shared 512 KiB pixel budget.
diversity_axes.notes: num_plays next to it is genuinely free - see its own axis.

diversity_axes.name: bit_depth
diversity_axes.why: Bit depth selects the sample-extraction path: sub-byte depths (1, 2, 4) run libpng's bit unpacking and pixel expansion, 8 runs the byte path, 16 runs the two-byte big-endian path with its own scaling and gamma arithmetic.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Different depths reach different png_do_unpack / 16-bit swap / row-stride code, change row_bytes and therefore the whole IDAT plaintext size, and gate which filter types are legal on a row.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit all five depths across the corpus, respecting the per-color-type subsets (1/2/4/8/16 for grayscale, 1/2/4/8 for indexed, 8/16 for truecolour and the alpha types) and deriving the IDAT plaintext from the chosen depth.
diversity_axes.notes: A wrong depth makes libpng refuse the file, but the five legal values are five distinct pipelines: dropping the sub-byte ones to keep generation simple would delete the unpacking code entirely.

diversity_axes.name: color_type
diversity_axes.why: Reconfigures the whole pixel pipeline: channel count, palette lookup versus direct colour, presence of alpha, and the shape of bKGD/sBIT/tRNS.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Type 0 runs the grayscale expand path, 2 the RGB path, 3 the palette lookup plus per-entry tRNS alpha path, 4 gray+alpha, 6 RGBA compositing. Each also selects a different bKGD and sBIT switch arm in this template (lines 195-262).
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit all five values across the corpus, with the bit-depth subset, the palette requirement and the conditional chunk shapes all derived from the chosen value.
diversity_axes.notes: Indexed (3) is the only value that pulls in PLTE, per-entry tRNS and hIST; do not treat it as the awkward case to skip.

diversity_axes.name: interlace_method
diversity_axes.why: Switches between one sequential row run and the seven Adam7 passes, a structurally different traversal of the pixel buffer.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng's png_read_start_row / png_read_finish_row pass arithmetic, the per-pass row offsets and the progressive-display callbacks only run for method 1; method 0 is the single-pass path.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit both values roughly evenly, and derive the IDAT plaintext layout (one row run versus seven pass runs) from the choice.
diversity_axes.notes: Adam7 files are where dimension diversity pays off twice: each of the seven passes has its own derived width and height.

diversity_axes.name: srgb_rendering_intent
diversity_axes.why: Four legal intents, each stored and reported differently, and the chunk's presence changes how libpng derives gamma and chromaticities.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng's sRGB handling installs default gamma/cHRM values and records the intent; with sRGB present an explicit gAMA or cHRM is cross-checked instead of trusted, which is a different branch.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit all four intents across the corpus, sometimes alongside gAMA/cHRM and sometimes not.
diversity_axes.notes: One byte per chunk, so covering all four costs almost nothing.

diversity_axes.name: itxt_compression_flag
diversity_axes.why: Two legal values that route the chunk's text through completely different code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Flag 0 copies UTF-8 out directly; flag 1 inflates it first, reaching the zlib path from an ancillary chunk and then the text callback with a decompressed buffer.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit both roughly evenly; when the flag is 1 wrap the free text in a zlib stream and set the chunk length from the finished stream.
diversity_axes.notes: Values above 1 are a benign error and are not part of the legal set.

diversity_axes.name: phys_unit_specifier
diversity_axes.why: Two legal values that make the same two numbers mean different things.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Unit 0 makes libpng treat the densities as an aspect ratio, unit 1 as pixels per metre; the unit also decides whether the values are converted for the consumer.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit both units with free density values in each case.
diversity_axes.notes: The template spells the first enumerator 'UnkownUnit' (line 223).

diversity_axes.name: splt_sample_depth
diversity_axes.why: Two legal depths that change the entry size and therefore the whole chunk layout.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng computes the entry size (6 bytes at depth 8, 10 at depth 16), validates the remaining length against it and stores the suggested palette accordingly.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit both depths with a free entry count inside the text budget and free entry bytes.
diversity_axes.notes: Any other depth is a benign error that drops the chunk.

diversity_axes.name: apng_dispose_op
diversity_axes.why: Three legal operations, each a separate branch in the frame-compositing code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: NONE leaves the canvas alone, BACKGROUND clears the frame region, PREVIOUS restores a saved copy - the last is the only way to reach libpng's frame save/restore buffer path.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit all three across the frames of the corpus, including several within one multi-frame file so the transitions between dispose operations run.
diversity_axes.notes: Dropping PREVIOUS because it needs a save buffer would delete that code entirely.

diversity_axes.name: apng_blend_op
diversity_axes.why: Two legal operations: overwrite the region, or alpha-composite over it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: OVER runs the per-pixel alpha compositing arithmetic on the frame region; SOURCE is a straight copy. They differ most when the frame carries alpha (color_type 4 or 6).
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit both, and pair OVER with alpha-bearing color types at least sometimes.
diversity_axes.notes: Values above 1 make libpng drop the frame.

diversity_axes.name: image_width
diversity_axes.why: Width sets the row stride, the filtered-bytes-per-row count, the sub-byte packing at depths 1/2/4 and the allocation size; narrow, wide, one-pixel and very wide images all take different paths through the unfilter and expand code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng computes rowbytes from width, samples per pixel and bit depth, allocates row buffers accordingly, and its Sub/Up/Average/Paeth unfilter loops run over rowbytes; the Adam7 pass widths are derived from it too. Width also decides how many IDAT chunks the derived stream is sliced into.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely across the uint32 span the output budget allows, including 1, prime widths, widths that are not a multiple of 8 (which matter at sub-byte depths), and very wide single-row images. Choose the width, then derive the IDAT payload from it.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Governed only by the 1 MiB file budget through the derived plaintext size (row_bytes * height). If a drawn width would make the derived stream exceed the remaining budget, redraw the width - never replace the field with a small value set so a precomputed payload fits.
diversity_axes.notes: Zero is the only value PNG declares invalid (excluded_values on the constraint entry). This axis is the exact place the GIF lesson applies: the payload is derived from the dimension, never the dimension from the payload.

diversity_axes.name: image_height
diversity_axes.why: Height is the row-loop bound and the number of filter-type bytes in the plaintext; it decides how many times the unfilter, expand and interlace code run.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng iterates rows 0..height-1 (or the seven Adam7 pass heights), calling png_read_filter_row per row; tall images also cross internal buffer boundaries that short images never reach.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely across the uint32 span the budget allows, including 1, 2, prime heights and very tall single-column images; derive the scanline count from whatever was drawn.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Same rule as width: the 1 MiB file budget is charged against the derived plaintext, and dimensions are redrawn rather than narrowed.
diversity_axes.notes: Zero excluded; everything else is legal.

diversity_axes.name: text_keyword
diversity_axes.why: Keyword and body lengths decide how many text chunks fit in the budget and drive libpng's keyword parsing, its 79-byte keyword handling and the label/body split.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng scans for the NUL separator, validates the keyword length benignly, copies the body and calls the text callback; different lengths reach different allocation and truncation branches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Random Latin-1 keywords (including the standard ones: Title, Author, Description, Copyright, Creation Time, Software, Disclaimer, Warning, Source, Comment) and random bodies from empty to budget-sized; exactly one NUL inside the chunk.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: 4 KiB total across all text chunks in a file, shared with zTXt, iTXt and sPLT.
diversity_axes.notes: The body length is derived from the chunk length minus the keyword, so it is free once the keyword and the budget are chosen.

diversity_axes.name: palette_red
diversity_axes.why: Palette colour bytes are the cheapest diversity in an indexed image: they change what every pixel expands to without touching any structural field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng expands indices through the palette and then applies gamma, sBIT scaling and tRNS alpha per entry, so different colour values take different branches in the scaling and transparency code.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Uniform random bytes across the whole 0-255 span for every entry of every file, including all-zero and all-FF entries.
diversity_axes.notes: No bound of any kind: these are colour values.

diversity_axes.name: chrm_chromaticity_x
diversity_axes.why: Chromaticity values feed the colour-management arithmetic; free values exercise it with different inputs, including degenerate ones.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng converts the 1/100000 fixed-point values to internal fixed point and checks them against representable limits, warning benignly when they are out of range - a branch only reachable with unusual values.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw across the uint32 span: the standard sRGB chromaticities, zeros, and large values alike. The chunk's 32-byte extent is fixed regardless.
diversity_axes.notes: Eight uint32 values per cHRM chunk (white, red, green, blue, each x and y) - all free.

diversity_axes.name: itxt_keyword_and_tags
diversity_axes.why: The three NUL-terminated strings in an iTXt chunk decide the derived extent of the text body and drive libpng's international-text parsing.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng parses keyword, compression flag, compression method, language tag and translated keyword in sequence, validating each separator; different string lengths reach different parsing and allocation branches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Random UTF-8 keywords, empty and non-empty language tags (en, en-GB, de-DE, x-private), random translated keywords; each NUL-terminated inside the chunk.
diversity_axes.notes: Empty strings are legal and are a distinct parsing case worth emitting.

diversity_axes.name: itxt_text_body
diversity_axes.why: The iTXt body is free UTF-8 text when uncompressed and free bytes inside a zlib stream when compressed, so it is diverse in both modes.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Uncompressed bodies go straight to the text callback; compressed ones run inflate first, then the callback with the expanded buffer - two different paths for the same field.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Random UTF-8 text of random length; when the compression flag is 1, wrap it in a zlib stream built from stored blocks and set the chunk length from the stream size.
diversity_axes.notes: The field stays Tier C even in compressed mode: the framing rule lives on the dependency, the bytes inside stay free.

diversity_axes.name: ztxt_keyword
diversity_axes.why: Free keyword text whose length derives the compressed body's extent.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng parses the keyword, checks the compression method byte and then inflates the body; keyword length affects the derived split point.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Random Latin-1 keywords, exactly one NUL inside the chunk.
diversity_axes.notes: Pair with a random uncompressed text body so the zlib payload differs every time.

diversity_axes.name: timestamp_fields
diversity_axes.why: Six free timestamp fields: no decoder gates on them, and they add header variation at zero depth cost.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng copies the seven bytes into its time structure and optionally converts them for the consumer; unusual values reach the conversion and bounds-warning code.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw each field across its whole declared type span (int16 year, byte month/day/hour/minute/second), including out-of-calendar values; the chunk stays 7 bytes either way.
diversity_axes.notes: The spec's nominal calendar limits are descriptive only and are deliberately not recorded as bounds on the constraint entries.

diversity_axes.name: background_colour
diversity_axes.why: The background value differs in shape by color_type and, for indexed images, indexes the palette; free values exercise the background handling with different inputs.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng stores the background and uses it when compositing or when the consumer asks for background expansion; an indexed background that names an existing entry runs the palette lookup, one that does not runs the benign warning path.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit the arm that matches color_type with free values across each field's whole type span; for indexed images include indices inside the palette and occasionally outside it.
diversity_axes.notes: Which of the five fields exists at all is derived from color_type - that is a format rule, not a narrowing of the values.

diversity_axes.name: phys_density
diversity_axes.why: Two free density numbers whose interpretation depends on the unit byte; they change nothing structural and are pure diversity.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng stores them and, for unit 1, converts pixels-per-metre for the consumer; unit 0 makes them an aspect ratio, which is a different code path.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw across the uint32 span, including equal X and Y (square pixels), unequal values, zero and very large values.
diversity_axes.notes: The 9-byte chunk extent is fixed regardless of the values.

diversity_axes.name: sbit_significant_bits
diversity_axes.why: Significant-bit counts change how libpng scales every sample, so free values here produce genuinely different pixel-processing arithmetic; thirteen fields across the five color-type arms all behave the same way.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng records the per-channel significant bits and, when they are below the sample depth, scales samples up during expansion - a path only reached with varied sBIT values. Out-of-bound values take the benign-error path instead.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit the arm that matches color_type, with each byte drawn freely across the byte span: equal values, unequal per-channel values, values equal to the bit depth, smaller values and occasionally larger ones.
diversity_axes.notes: These fields look like bit depths and invite a value set of {8}; that is exactly the narrowing this axis forbids. The only relation the format imposes (value <= sample depth) is recorded as a dependency.

diversity_axes.name: splt_palette_name
diversity_axes.why: A free name that lets several sPLT chunks coexist and drives libpng's duplicate-name handling.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng stores each suggested palette under its name and reports a benign error on duplicates, so repeated and duplicate names reach different branches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Random names, sometimes repeated within a file, NUL-terminated inside the chunk.
diversity_axes.notes: Multiple sPLT chunks are legal, unlike most ancillary chunks.

diversity_axes.name: splt_entry_table
diversity_axes.why: Opaque entry bytes whose count is derived from the chunk length and sample depth; the bytes themselves are free diversity.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng validates the extent against the entry size and then copies the table, so different entry counts and depths reach different validation and allocation branches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose a free entry count, emit count * (6 or 10) bytes of random data, and set the chunk length from name + sample-depth byte + table.
diversity_axes.notes: Only the multiple-of-entry-size relation is a format rule (dependency); the byte values are unconstrained.

diversity_axes.name: apng_play_count
diversity_axes.why: A loop count nothing validates: free values add animation-header variation at no cost.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng stores it for the consumer; 0 means loop forever, which is a distinct value in the animation control path.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw across the uint32 span, including 0.
diversity_axes.notes: Do not confuse with num_frames, which is derived from the fcTL count.

diversity_axes.name: frame_width
diversity_axes.why: Per-frame width sets the frame's row stride and blit bounds; frames of differing width make the compositor run with different rectangles.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng derives the frame's rowbytes and composite region from it, so each distinct width is a different traversal of the frame buffer.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely subject only to x_offset + width <= IHDR.width, and derive the frame's fdAT payload from the result.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Charged through the derived frame payload inside the shared 512 KiB pixel budget.
diversity_axes.notes: Never pin frame geometry to a small set to suit a precomputed payload.

diversity_axes.name: frame_height
diversity_axes.why: Per-frame height is the frame's row-loop bound.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng iterates the frame's rows when unfiltering and compositing; differing heights change how many times that runs per frame.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely subject only to y_offset + height <= IHDR.height, then derive the frame payload.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Charged through the derived frame payload inside the shared pixel budget.
diversity_axes.notes: Same derive-don't-shrink rule as the image dimensions.

diversity_axes.name: frame_offset
diversity_axes.why: Offsets place the frame region inside the canvas; different offsets make the compositor copy to different parts of the buffer.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng computes the destination rectangle from the offsets, so non-zero and edge-flush placements reach different bounds arithmetic than a zero offset.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw freely subject to the containment rule, including 0, edge-flush and interior placements.
diversity_axes.notes: Full-canvas frames (offset 0, size equal to the IHDR size) and small interior frames are both worth emitting.

diversity_axes.name: frame_delay
diversity_axes.why: Two free timing numbers per frame; no decoder gates on them and they vary the animation control data.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libpng stores the fraction and applies the delay_den == 0 default of 100, which is a distinct branch.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw both across their int16 span, including delay_den 0 to reach the hundredths-of-a-second default.
diversity_axes.notes: Durations are Tier C by definition; no bound is recorded anywhere for them.
